verdict_label: Fine for kids, odd for adults
explanation: China doesn't carry the strict Buddhist head-sacredness taboo found in Thailand or Laos; it's common, even affectionate, for an adult to pat a child's head. Touching an adult's or stranger's head, though, is still generally seen as an invasive overstep of personal space rather than a deep spiritual offense.
local_tip: Patting a friend's or stranger's child on the head as a friendly gesture is generally fine; avoid doing the same to adults you don't know well.

also_check.note: The head is considered the most sacred part of the body in Buddhist belief, so touching anyone's head, including a child's, is a serious offense.
Touching an elder's or stranger's head is disrespectful, though patting a child's head is often acceptable among close family.
Patting a child's head or a close friend's head affectionately is generally seen as warm rather than offensive.
